newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - New Westinghouse Electric faces old problems.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - New Westinghouse Electric faces old problems.

text.p: The new industrial company to be formed by Westinghouse Electric Corp's split will face old problems and has a formidable task in revamping lackluster operations to make itself attractive to investors, analysts said Wednesday.
But they said the new company could be investment-worthy if it pursued lucrative overseas contracts for its power business and used its one money-making unit, Thermo King, as an earnings booster.
"There's nothing there to draw investors, except the potential that (the new company) can turn around," said Greg Drahuschak at Janney Montgomery Scott.

In a historical move, Westinghouse said Wednesday it will separate its $4.6 billion industrial operations from its media operations by way of a tax-free shareholder spinoff, breaking up a century-old Pittsburgh conglomerate.

The industrial company will be called Westinghouse Electric Co (WELCO) and will be based in Pittsburgh, while the media company will be based in New York. The companies will have separate directors, management, and stock.
WELCO will consist of four units: power generation, energy systems, government operations and Thermo King, a refrigerated transportation business and the only unit that has been profitable.
Power generation, the largest unit, has been struggling with sluggish pricing despite strong demand. The unit posted a $16 million operating loss last year.
Moreover, energy systems and government operations have been facing shrinking markets.
"The biggest earnings potential (for WELCO) is in overseas projects for the power business," Drahuschak said.
"Westinghouse has been pursuing those projects and will continue to do so, I'm sure. The company has to have patience and hopefully enough cash flow until it turns around."

Westinghouse said it will provide cash funding for WELCO via a public offering of 20 percent of Thermo King's stock. Analysts had speculated in recent months that Westinghouse would sell Thermo King, but they said it is the one industrial unit that will give WELCO turnaround potential.
"Thermo King is a good business; it's a profitable business," said Kent Newcomb at A.G. Edwards. "That certainly gives the spinoff upside potential.
"But their power business has been struggling and that's not going to change overnight."

As part of the split, Westinghouse will eliminate approximately 1,100 positions from energy systems and power generation to reduce overhead and operating costs. To further cut costs, the company is divesting its security systems business. "I think the cost-cutting that needed to be done, was done with those moves," Drahuschak said.
While the media company's stock could trade above the company's current share value, analysts said the industrial stock will likely trade around $3 or $4 per share.

Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan will head the media company but Westinghouse declined to comment on who may be named to head WELCO. Analysts said Westinghouse could hire internally -- the industrial operations currently are run by Executive Vice President Fran Harvey -- or hire outside talent.
